claim: Fap7 is a conserved ATPase that organizes interactions between neighboring r-proteins uS11 and eS26 prior to their delivery to the 90S.
source: Here, we reveal that a conserved ATPase, Fap7, organizes interactions between neighboring r-proteins uS11 and eS26 prior to their delivery to the earliest ribosome precursor, the 90S.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by multiple experimental data throughout the manuscript including in vitro binding assays and genetic studies.

claim: uS11 only when bound to Fap7 becomes competent to recruit eS26 through tertiary contacts found between these r-proteins on the mature ribosome.
source: In vitro, uS11 only when bound to Fap7 becomes competent to recruit eS26 through tertiary contacts found between these r-proteins on the mature ribosome.
evidence: Supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 3A demonstrating that GST-Fap7:uS11 complex efficiently recruited eS26, while GST-uS11 alone did not.

claim: Fap7 ATPase activity unloads the uS11:eS26 subcomplex onto its rRNA binding site.
source: Subsequently, Fap7 ATPase activity unloads the uS11:eS26 subcomplex onto its rRNA binding site, and therefore ensures stoichiometric integration of these r-proteins into the 90S.
evidence: Supported by in vitro data in Figure 5B showing that Fap7 ATPase activity is required to load uS11:eS26 onto H23 rRNA, while the catalytically inactive Fap7-2 mutant cannot.

claim: Fap7-depletion in vivo renders uS11 susceptible to proteolysis.
source: Fap7-depletion in vivo renders uS11 susceptible to proteolysis, and precludes eS26 incorporation into the 90S.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figure 2H showing strongly reduced uS11 protein levels in Fap7-depleted cells.

claim: Fap7-depletion precludes eS26 incorporation into the 90S.
source: Fap7-depletion in vivo renders uS11 susceptible to proteolysis, and precludes eS26 incorporation into the 90S.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figure 2F showing that eS26 poorly co-enriched with Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted cells.

claim: The eukaryotic large 60S ribosomal subunit contains three rRNAs (25S, 5.8S, 5S) and 46 r-proteins.
source: In eukaryotes, the large 60S subunit contains three rRNAs (25S, 5.8S, 5S) and 46 r-proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosome composition, cited with references to structural studies (Klinge et al., 2011; Rabl et al., 2011).

claim: The eukaryotic small 40S ribosomal subunit contains a single rRNA (18S) and 33 r-proteins.
source: The small 40S subunit contains a single rRNA (18S) and 33 r-proteins (Klinge et al., 2011; Rabl et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosome composition, cited with references to structural studies.

claim: More than 200 conserved assembly factors drive eukaryotic ribosome production.
source: A coordinated effort of all three transcriptional machineries (RNA polymerases I, II and III) and >200 conserved assembly factors drives eukaryotic ribosome production (de la Cruz et al., 2015; Woolford and Baserga, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosome assembly, supported by citations to review articles.

claim: RNA polymerase I driven production of 35S pre-rRNA initiates eukaryotic ribosome assembly in the nucleolus.
source: RNA polymerase I driven production of 35S pre-rRNA initiates eukaryotic ribosome assembly in the nucleolus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the initiation of ribosome assembly.

claim: The emerging pre-rRNA associates with small subunit r-proteins and ~100 assembly factors to form the earliest precursor, the 90S.
source: The emerging pre-rRNA associates with small subunit r-proteins, and ~100 assembly factors to form the earliest precursor, the 90S (Dragon et al., 2002; Grandi et al., 2002; Kos and Tollervey, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about 90S formation, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A 40S pre-ribosome undergoes few compositional changes as it travels through the nucleoplasm and is rapidly exported into the cytoplasm.
source: A 40S pre-ribosome undergoes few compositional changes as it travels through the nucleoplasm and is rapidly exported into the cytoplasm (Grandi et al., 2002; Schäfer et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge about 40S pre-ribosome maturation, supported by citations.

claim: A 60S pre-ribosome transiently interacts with ~80 assembly factors as it travels towards the nuclear periphery.
source: In contrast, a 60S pre-ribosome transiently interacts with ~80 assembly factors, as it travels towards the nuclear periphery (Bassler et al., 2001; Fatica et al., 2002; Harnpicharnchai et al., 2001; Nissan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about 60S pre-ribosome maturation, supported by citations.

claim: Assembly factors are released from ribosome precursors possibly through the action of >50 energy-consuming RNA helicases, AAA-ATPases, ABC-ATPases and GTPases.
source: At distinct stages, assembly factors are released from ribosome precursors possibly through the action of >50 energy-consuming RNA helicases, AAA-ATPases, ABC-ATPases and GTPases (Kressler et al., 2010; Panse and Johnson, 2010; Strunk and Karbstein, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of energy-consuming enzymes in ribosome assembly, supported by citations and indicated as speculative with 'possibly'.

claim: Cytoplasmic maturation of the 40S pre-ribosome requires endonucleolytic cleavage of the 20S pre-rRNA at site D to generate the 3' end of mature 18S rRNA.
source: Cytoplasmic maturation of the 40S pre-ribosome requires endonucleolytic cleavage of the 20S pre-rRNA at site D to generate the 3' end of mature 18S rRNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cytoplasmic maturation of 40S pre-ribosomes.

claim: The endonuclease Nob1 catalyzes the cleavage of 20S pre-rRNA at site D.
source: This step is catalyzed by the endonuclease Nob1 (Fatica et al., 2004; Lamanna and Karbstein, 2009; Pertschy et al., 2009)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: 20S pre-rRNA cleavage is thought to occur within an 80S-like particle formed upon the interaction of a 40S pre-ribosome with a mature 60S subunit.
source: and is thought to occur within an 80S-like particle formed upon the interaction of a 40S pre-ribosome with a mature 60S subunit (Lebaron et al., 2012; Strunk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations, indicated by 'is thought to occur'.

claim: r-proteins uS11 and eS26 are essential for endonucleolytic cleavage of 20S pre-rRNA.
source: Additionally, r-proteins uS11 and eS26 (yeast Rps14a/b and Rps26a/b; nomenclature according to Ban et al., 2014) are essential for endonucleolytic cleavage of 20S pre-rRNA (Jakovljevic et al., 2004; Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: eS26 clamps the 3' end of 18S rRNA and directly contacts its neighboring r-protein uS11.
source: eS26 clamps the 3' end of 18S rRNA and directly contacts its neighboring r-protein uS11.
evidence: This is structural knowledge about the mature ribosome, likely inferred from structural studies.

claim: Depletion of Tsr2 or the ATPase Fap7 impairs cytoplasmic processing of 20S pre-rRNA.
source: Depletion of Tsr2 or the ATPase Fap7, the binding partners of eS26 and uS11, respectively, also impairs cytoplasmic processing of 20S pre-rRNA (Granneman et al., 2005; Schütz et al., 2014; Strunk et al., 2012)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Within 90 min in yeast, the majority of ~14 million newly synthesized r-proteins are targeted to the nuclear compartment by the import machinery for incorporation into pre-ribosomal particles.
source: In yeast, within 90 min, the majority of ~14 million newly synthesized r-proteins are targeted to the nuclear compartment by the import machinery for incorporation into pre-ribosomal particles (Warner, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about r-protein import kinetics, supported by citation.

claim: r-proteins contain large unstructured regions that are prone to non-specific interactions with nucleic acids and proteolytic degradation in their non-assembled state.
source: r-proteins contain large unstructured regions that are prone to non-specific interactions with nucleic acids and proteolytic degradation in their non-assembled state (Jäkel and Görlich, 1998; Jäkel et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about r-protein properties, supported by citations.

claim: A subset of newly synthesized r-proteins employ dedicated chaperones that bind them in the cytoplasm and co-coordinate their nuclear import.
source: To overcome this logistical challenge, a subset of newly synthesized r-proteins employ dedicated chaperones that bind them in the cytoplasm and co-coordinate their nuclear import (Mitterer et al., 2016; Pausch et al., 2015; Pillet et al., 2015; Stelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about r-protein chaperones, supported by citations.

claim: eS26 directly recruits multiple importins for its transport to the nucleus.
source: In this case, eS26, like a typical import cargo, directly recruits multiple importins for its transport to the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, as indicated by the citation (Schütz et al., 2014).

claim: After reaching the nuclear compartment, eS26 is extracted from the importin by the escortin Tsr2 without the aid of RanGTP.
source: However, unlike a typical import cargo, after reaching the nuclear compartment, eS26 is extracted from the importin by an unloading factor, the escortin Tsr2, without the aid of RanGTP.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, as indicated by the citation (Schütz et al., 2014).

claim: Once bound to Tsr2, eS26 is shielded from proteolysis, enabling its safe transfer to the 90S.
source: Once bound to Tsr2, eS26 is shielded from proteolysis, enabling its safe transfer to the 90S.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, as indicated by the citation (Schütz et al., 2014).

claim: Tsr2-depleted cells are viable but severely impaired in growth.
source: While eS26 is essential for yeast cell viability, Tsr2-depleted cells are viable, but severely impaired in growth (Figure 1A; Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1A and cited from previous work.

claim: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 rescues the slow growth of Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 together restored impaired growth of the PGAL1-TSR2 mutant to nearly WT rates (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 rescues the 20S pre-rRNA processing defect of Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Co-overexpressing FAP7 and uS11 significantly reduced 20S pre-RNA levels in these cells (Figure 1C, compare lanes 1 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 1C and FISH data in Figure 1B.

claim: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 restores eS26 protein levels in Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 in Tsr2-depleted cells restored eS26 protein levels to nearly WT levels as judged by Western analyses of whole cell extracts (WCEs) (Figure 1D, compare lanes 1 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 restores eS26 co-enrichment with Enp1-TAP in Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 in these cells restored eS26 co-enrichment with Enp1-TAP to nearly WT levels (Figure 1E, compare lanes 1 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification and Western blot data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Fap7 is a nuclear localized protein.
source: The nuclear localized Fap7 (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fap7 was initially isolated in a genetic screen as a factor required for Pos9-driven transcription of genes upon oxidative stress.
source: The nuclear localized Fap7 (Figure 2A) was initially isolated in a genetic screen as a factor required for Pos9-driven transcription of genes upon oxidative stress (Juhnke et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: Fap7 is an energy-consuming enzyme that is not a structural component of pre-ribosomes but directly binds the r-protein uS11.
source: Subsequently, it was identified as an energy-consuming enzyme that is not a structural component of pre-ribosomes, but directly binds the r-protein uS11 (Granneman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: uS11 alone, but not Fap7, co-enriched with the 90S and 40S pre-ribosomes.
source: Consistent with these studies, we found that uS11 alone, but not Fap7, co-enriched with the 90S and 40S pre-ribosomes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification and Western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fap7-depletion does not impair export of 40S pre-ribosomes.
source: Moreover, like the escortin Tsr2, Fap7-depletion did not impair export of 40S pre-ribosomes (Figure 2C; Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2C showing cytoplasmic localization of uS5-GFP in Fap7-depleted cells.

claim: 40S pre-ribosomes exported from Fap7-depleted cells fail to process immature 20S pre-rRNA into mature 18S rRNA.
source: However, these exported pre-ribosomes failed to process immature 20S pre-rRNA into mature 18S rRNA (Figure 2D; Granneman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2D and cited from previous work.

claim: Co-overexpression of TSR2 and RPS26a does not rescue the lethality of the Fap7-depletion strain.
source: While co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS11 restored impaired growth of Tsr2-depleted cells to nearly WT rates, co-overexpression of TSR2 and RPS26a, did not rescue the lethality of the Fap7-depletion strain (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Both uS11 and eS26 poorly co-enriched with Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted cells.
source: Western analyses revealed that both uS11 and eS26 poorly co-enriched with the Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted cells (Figure 2F)
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification and Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Both uS11 and eS26 poorly co-enriched with Enp1-TAP isolated from Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Western analyses revealed that both uS11 and eS26 poorly co-enriched with the Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted cells (Figure 2F) and from Tsr2-depleted cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification and Western blot data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: r-proteins uS3 and uS7 efficiently co-enriched with Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted and Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: In contrast, r-proteins uS3 and uS7 efficiently co-enriched with Enp1-TAP isolated from Fap7-depleted (Figure 2F) and Tsr2-depleted cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by TAP purification and Western blot data shown in Figures 2F and 2G.

claim: Incorporation of eS26 and uS11 into the pre-ribosome requires both Fap7 and Tsr2.
source: We conclude that incorporation of eS26 and uS11 into the pre-ribosome requires both Fap7 and Tsr2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing poor co-enrichment of both proteins with pre-ribosomes when either Fap7 or Tsr2 is depleted.

claim: Fap7-depletion strongly reduces uS11 protein levels in whole cell extracts but eS26 protein levels remain similar to WT levels.
source: Fap7-depletion strongly reduced uS11 protein levels in WCEs, but eS26 protein levels were very similar to WT levels (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Fap7-depletion does not affect eS26 protein stability in vivo but impairs its targeting to the pre-ribosome.
source: These data show that Fap7-depletion does not affect eS26 protein stability in vivo, but impairs its targeting to the pre-ribosome (Figure 2F and H).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that eS26 protein levels are normal in whole cell extracts but poorly co-enrich with pre-ribosomes in Fap7-depleted cells.

claim: Tsr2-depleted cells show strongly reduced levels of eS26 in whole cell extracts.
source: Consistent with previous studies, Tsr2-depleted cells showed strongly reduced levels of eS26 in WCEs (Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2I and cited from previous work.

claim: uS11 protein levels are similar to WT levels in Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: uS11 protein levels were very similar to WT levels in these extracts (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Tsr2-depletion does not influence uS11 protein stability in vivo but impairs its targeting to the pre-ribosome.
source: These data show that Tsr2-depletion does not influence uS11 protein stability in vivo, but impairs its targeting to the pre-ribosome (Figure 2G and I).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that uS11 protein levels are normal in whole cell extracts but poorly co-enrich with pre-ribosomes in Tsr2-depleted cells.

claim: uS11 and eS26 are dependent upon each other for their incorporation into the 90S.
source: Based on all these studies, we suggest that uS11 and eS26 are dependent upon each other for their incorporation into the 90S.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing that depletion of factors affecting one protein also affects incorporation of the other.

claim: A preformed GST-Fap7:uS11 complex efficiently recruited eS26 in vitro.
source: These studies revealed that a preformed GST-Fap7:uS11 complex efficiently recruited eS26 (Figure 3A, lane 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: GST-Fap7 alone does not recruit eS26.
source: GST-Fap7 alone did not recruit eS26 (Figure 3A, lane 5).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Neither GST-Fap7 nor GST-Fap7:uS11 interacts with the Tsr2:eS26 complex.
source: Neither GST-Fap7 nor GST-Fap7:uS11 interacted with the Tsr2:eS26 complex (Figure 3A, lane 3 and 6).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: GST-uS11 does not interact with eS26 and the Tsr2:eS26 complex.
source: GST-uS11 did not interact with eS26 and the Tsr2:eS26 complex (Figure 3A, lane 11 and 12).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: uS11 only in complex with Fap7 is competent to recruit eS26.
source: Based on these studies, we conclude that uS11 only in complex with Fap7 is competent to recruit eS26.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from in vitro binding assays showing that GST-Fap7:uS11 recruits eS26 while GST-uS11 alone does not.

claim: On the mature 40S subunit, uS11 and eS26 are neighbors and contact each other through a network of conserved salt-bridges and hydrogen bonds.
source: On the mature 40S subunit, uS11 and eS26 are neighbors and contact each other through a network of conserved salt-bridges and hydrogen bonds (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is structural knowledge derived from the mature ribosome structure, as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: uS11 R103/R107 and eS26 D52 form salt-bridge contacts on the mature 40S subunit.
source: These include: (1) R103 / R107 on uS11 and D52 on eS26, (2) R114 on uS11 and Y59 / Y62 on eS26.
evidence: This is structural knowledge shown in Figure 3B.

claim: uS11 R114 and eS26 Y59/Y62 form contacts on the mature 40S subunit.
source: These include: (1) R103 / R107 on uS11 and D52 on eS26, (2) R114 on uS11 and Y59 / Y62 on eS26.
evidence: This is structural knowledge shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The uS113R mutant protein is not impaired in binding Fap7.
source: The uS113R mutant protein was not impaired in binding Fap7 (Figure 3C, lane 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The mutant GST-Fap7:uS113R heterodimer is significantly impaired in recruiting eS26.
source: However, the mutant GST-Fap7:uS113R heterodimer was significantly impaired in recruiting eS26 (Figure 3C, lane 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: eS26 recruitment to the Fap7:uS11 complex involves native-like tertiary contacts found between these r-proteins on the mature 40S subunit.
source: These data support the notion that eS26 recruitment to the Fap7:uS11 complex involves native-like tertiary contacts found between these r-proteins on the mature 40S subunit.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutations disrupting these contacts impair eS26 recruitment to the Fap7:uS11 complex.

claim: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS113R does not rescue the growth of Tsr2-depleted cells.
source: Co-overexpression of FAP7 and uS113R did not rescue the growth and different PGAL1-TSR2-associated phenotypes such as impaired 20S pre-rRNA processing, eS26 protein levels and recruitment to the pre-ribosome (Figure 3E and F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 3D and other phenotypic analyses.

claim: Robust interactions between uS11 and eS26 are critical to stabilize and deliver eS26 to the 90S when Tsr2 is absent.
source: Based on these functional studies, we conclude that robust interactions between uS11 and eS26 are critical to stabilize and deliver eS26 to the 90S, when Tsr2 is absent.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that mutations disrupting uS11-eS26 interactions prevent rescue of Tsr2-depletion phenotypes.

claim: The Fap7-2 Walker B mutant binds uS11 efficiently.
source: While, the Fap7-2 Walker B mutant bound uS11 efficiently (Figure 4A, right panel), its ATPase activity could not be stimulated and was very similar to Fap7 activity alone (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by protein purification data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The Fap7-2 Walker B mutant's ATPase activity cannot be stimulated by uS11 binding.
source: While, the Fap7-2 Walker B mutant bound uS11 efficiently (Figure 4A, right panel), its ATPase activity could not be stimulated and was very similar to Fap7 activity alone (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Fap7 alone shows no significant ATPase activity.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Hellmich et al., 2013; Loc'h et al., 2014), Fap7 alone shows no significant ATPase activity (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 4B and cited from previous studies.

claim: Binding to uS11 stimulates Fap7 ATPase activity.
source: However, binding to uS11 stimulates its ATPase activity (Hellmich et al., 2013) as indicated by an increase in ADP formation over time.
evidence: This is supported by ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 4B and cited from previous studies.

claim: The Fap7-2 Walker B mutant is severely impaired in ATP binding.
source: These analyses revealed that the Fap7-2 Walker B mutant is severely impaired in ATP binding, as its fluorescence emission spectrum, unlike wild-type Fap7, remained similar to mant-ATP alone (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by ATP binding assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The impaired ATPase activity of the Fap7-2 mutant arises from its inability to bind ATP.
source: Thus, the impaired ATPase activity of the Fap7-2 mutant seems to arise from its inability to bind ATP.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fap7-2 cannot bind ATP and also lacks ATPase activity.

claim: Co-overexpression of fap7-2 and uS11 does not rescue the growth impairment of the PGAL1-TSR2 mutant.
source: These analyses revealed that co-overexpression of fap7-2 and uS11 was unable to rescue the growth impairment of the PGAL1-TSR2 mutant (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Co-overexpression of uS11 and a catalytically active FAP7 is critical to compensate the functional requirement of Tsr2 in vivo.
source: Based on all these data, we conclude that co-overexpression of uS11 and a catalytically active FAP7 is critical to compensate the functional requirement of Tsr2 in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that the catalytically inactive fap7-2 mutant cannot rescue Tsr2-depletion phenotypes.

claim: The catalytic activity of Fap7 regulates the interaction of uS11 with its 18S rRNA binding site helix 23 (H23) in vitro.
source: Two studies had revealed that the catalytic activity of Fap7 regulates the interaction of uS11 with its 18S rRNA binding site helix 23 (H23) in vitro (Hellmich et al., 2013; Loc'h et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Fap7 and eS26 are efficiently recruited to GST-uS11 in the absence of ATP.
source: These interaction studies revealed that Fap7 and eS26 were efficiently recruited to GST-uS11 in the absence of ATP (Figure 5B, lane 4).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: H23 rRNA is hardly recruited to the Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex in the absence of ATP.
source: Consistent with the reported RNA mimic function for Fap7 (Loc'h et al., 2014), H23 rRNA was hardly recruited to the Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex in the absence of ATP (Figure 5B, lane 8).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B and consistent with previous structural studies.

claim: GST-uS11 efficiently loads eS26 and H23 rRNA in the presence of catalytically active Fap7 and ATP.
source: Notably, GST-uS11 was efficient in loading eS26 and H23 rRNA in the presence of catalytically active Fap7 and ATP (Figure 5B, lane 9).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: GST-uS11 fails to recruit H23 rRNA in the presence of catalytically inactive Fap7-2 mutant.
source: GST-uS11 failed to recruit H23 rRNA in the presence of a catalytically inactive Fap7-2 mutant, and Fap7 loaded with the non-hydrolysable ATP analog AMPPNP (Figure 5B, lanes 10–13).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: GST-uS11 fails to recruit H23 rRNA in the presence of Fap7 loaded with the non-hydrolysable ATP analog AMPPNP.
source: GST-uS11 failed to recruit H23 rRNA in the presence of a catalytically inactive Fap7-2 mutant, and Fap7 loaded with the non-hydrolysable ATP analog AMPPNP (Figure 5B, lanes 10–13).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: GST-eS26 alone does not detectably bind H23 rRNA.
source: Recruitment of H23 rRNA to the GST-uS11:eS26 complex is not due to bound eS26, since GST-eS26 alone did not detectably bind H23 rRNA (Figure 5C, lane 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Nearly identical levels of H23 rRNA are recruited to GST-uS11 and GST-uS11:eS26 complexes in the presence of Fap7 and ATP.
source: Further, nearly identical levels of H23 rRNA were recruited to GST-uS11 and GST-uS11:eS26 complexes, in the presence of Fap7 and ATP (Figure 5C, compare lanes 5 and 7).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Fap7 orchestrates the formation of an uS11:eS26 complex and its ATPase activity facilitates loading of this prefabricated r-protein subcomplex onto H23 rRNA.
source: Altogether, these data show that Fap7 orchestrates the formation of an uS11:eS26 complex, and its ATPase activity facilitates loading of this prefabricated r-protein subcomplex onto H23 rRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple in vitro binding assays showing Fap7-dependent complex formation and ATP-dependent RNA loading.

claim: uS11-GFP localizes to the nucleus.
source: uS11-GFP localized to the nucleus indicating that the fusion protein was competent to interact with nuclear import machinery, but as expected it is unable to complement the lethality of the uS11-deletion strain (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: uS11-GFP is unable to complement the lethality of the uS11-deletion strain.
source: uS11-GFP localized to the nucleus indicating that the fusion protein was competent to interact with nuclear import machinery, but as expected it is unable to complement the lethality of the uS11-deletion strain (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by complementation assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Nuclear uptake of uS11-GFP is specifically impaired in the pse1-1 mutant and pse1-1/kap104∆ double mutant.
source: Nuclear uptake of uS11-GFP was specifically impaired in the pse1-1 mutant and pse1-1/kap104∆ double mutant, but not in other tested importin mutants such as kap104∆, kap123∆, msn5∆, kap114∆/sxm1∆ and kap120∆/sxm1∆/nmd5∆.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: uS11 employs primarily Pse1 for nuclear targeting.
source: These in vivo data suggest that uS11 employs primarily Pse1 for nuclear targeting.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that nuclear uptake of uS11-GFP is impaired specifically in pse1 mutants.

claim: Importins Pse1 and Kap104 efficiently recruit the Fap7:uS11 complex but not Fap7 alone.
source: However, we found that importins Pse1 and Kap104 efficiently recruited the Fap7:uS11 complex, but not Fap7 alone (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: uS11 can function as an adaptor to transport Fap7 to the nucleus via a 'piggyback' mechanism.
source: suggesting that uS11 can function as an adaptor to transport Fap7 to the nucleus via a 'piggyback' mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Fap7:uS11 complex binds importins while Fap7 alone does not bind these importins efficiently.

claim: Fap7 alone binds to Kap123 and Msn5.
source: Fap7 alone bound to Kap123 and Msn5 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, upper panel).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: RanGTP efficiently dissociates Fap7:uS11 from Pse1.
source: Indeed, incubation with RanGTP efficiently dissociated Fap7:uS11 from Pse1 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Incubation of the Fap7:uS11 complex with importins Kap95, Kap114, Pdr6 and Kap123 results in dissociation of the Fap7:uS11 heterodimer with only uS11 remaining bound to the importin.
source: Surprisingly, incubation of the Fap7:uS11 complex with importins Kap95, Kap114, Pdr6 and Kap123, resulted in the dissociation of the Fap7:uS11 heterodimer with only uS11 remaining bound to the importin (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, upper panel), suggesting overlapping sites for Fap7 and these importins for binding to uS11.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Nuclear localization of GFP-Fap7 is not altered in different importin mutants tested.
source: However, nuclear localization of GFP-Fap7 was not altered in different importin mutants (pse1-1, kap104∆, pse1-1/kap104∆, kap123∆, msn5∆, kap114∆/sxm1∆ and kap120∆/sxm1∆/nmd5∆) that we tested.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GFP-Fap7 is efficiently targeted to the nucleus in an uS11-depleted strain.
source: In addition, GFP-Fap7 was efficiently targeted to the nucleus in an uS11-depleted strain (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: uS11 and Fap7 can be independently transported by multiple importins to the nuclear compartment.
source: suggesting that uS11 and Fap7 can be independently transported by multiple importins to the nuclear compartment.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GFP-Fap7 nuclear localization is not impaired in various importin mutants or upon uS11 depletion.

claim: Both GFP-Fap7 and uS11-GFP mislocalize to the cytoplasm in prp20-1 and rna1-1 mutants at restrictive temperatures.
source: Consistent with Ran-cycle requirement, both GFP-Fap7 and uS11-GFP mislocalized to the cytoplasm in prp20-1 and rna1-1 mutants at restrictive temperatures of 37°C (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Prp20 is the Ran-GEF (GDP/GTP-exchange factor) of Ran in yeast.
source: Prp20 (Ran-GEF) and Rna1 (Ran-GAP) are the GDP/GTP-exchange and GTPase-activating factors of Ran (Gsp1 in yeast), respectively (Görlich and Kutay, 1999; Vetter and Wittinghofer, 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ran cycle, supported by citations.

claim: Rna1 is the Ran-GAP (GTPase-activating factor) of Ran in yeast.
source: Prp20 (Ran-GEF) and Rna1 (Ran-GAP) are the GDP/GTP-exchange and GTPase-activating factors of Ran (Gsp1 in yeast), respectively (Görlich and Kutay, 1999; Vetter and Wittinghofer, 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ran cycle, supported by citations.

claim: Pse1 functions as the major importin for uS11.
source: Based on the above cell-biological and biochemical studies, we suggest that Pse1 functions as the major importin for uS11.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from multiple lines of evidence including in vivo localization studies and in vitro binding assays.

claim: Fap7 enters the nucleus either bound directly to Kap123, Msn5 and Kap104 or indirectly to Pse1 via uS11.
source: Fap7 enters the nucleus either bound directly to Kap123, Msn5 and Kap104 or indirectly to Pse1 via uS11.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from in vitro binding assays and in vivo localization studies.

claim: Disruption of the Ran gradient precludes nuclear uptake of both uS11 and Fap7.
source: Consistent with importin-facilitated entry, disruption of the Ran gradient precludes nuclear uptake of both uS11 and Fap7.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that both proteins mislocalize to the cytoplasm in prp20-1 and rna1-1 mutants.

claim: An importin:eS26 complex is inefficiently dissociated upon incubation with RanGTP in vitro.
source: Previously, we reported that an importin:eS26 complex is inefficiently dissociated upon incubation with RanGTP in vitro (Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: Tsr2 is able to unload eS26 from the importin:eS26 complex in a RanGTP-independent manner.
source: Instead, Tsr2 was able to unload eS26 from the importin:eS26 complex in a RanGTP-independent manner (Schütz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: Fap7:uS11 does not release eS26 from Pse1 in the absence of RanGTP.
source: These analyses revealed that Fap7:uS11 did not release eS26 from Pse1. Instead, Fap7:uS11 was recruited to the GST-Pse1:eS26 resin (Figure 7A, lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Fap7:uS11 is recruited to the GST-Pse1:eS26 complex.
source: These analyses revealed that Fap7:uS11 did not release eS26 from Pse1. Instead, Fap7:uS11 was recruited to the GST-Pse1:eS26 resin (Figure 7A, lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: eS26 is efficiently released from GST-Pse1:eS26:Fap7:uS11 complex after incubation with RanGTP.
source: Intriguingly, eS26 was efficiently released after incubating this resin with RanGTP (Figure 7B, compare lanes 3 and 5).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The GST-Pse1:eS26 complex becomes sensitive to RanGTP-dependent disassembly due to the recruitment of the Fap7:uS11 complex.
source: These data suggest that the GST-Pse1:eS26 complex becomes sensitive to RanGTP-dependent disassembly possibly due to the recruitment of the Fap7:uS11 complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that eS26 is released from Pse1 by RanGTP only after Fap7:uS11 recruitment.

claim: Treatment with the mutant Fap7:uS113R complex does not render GST-Pse1:eS26 susceptible to RanGTP disassembly.
source: These studies revealed that, unlike the wild-type Fap7:uS11 complex, treatment with the mutant Fap7:uS113R complex did not render GST-Pse1:eS26 susceptible to RanGTP disassembly (Figure 7B, compare lanes 5 and 7).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Recruitment of Fap7:uS11 to the Pse1:eS26 complex through tertiary contacts renders eS26 release from Pse1 RanGTP sensitive.
source: These data support the idea that recruitment of Fap7:uS11 to the Pse1:eS26 complex through tertiary contacts renders eS26 release from Pse1 RanGTP sensitive.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that wild-type Fap7:uS11 but not the mutant Fap7:uS113R enables RanGTP-dependent eS26 release.

claim: Every 30 ms, a growing budding yeast cell assembles a functional ribosome by precisely targeting 79 different r-proteins to their cognate RNA binding site.
source: Every 30 ms, a growing budding yeast cell assembles a functional ribosome by precisely targeting 79 different r-proteins to their cognate RNA binding site (Warner, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosome assembly kinetics, supported by citation.

claim: The ATPase Fap7 promotes tertiary interactions between eS26 and uS11 and then concurrently assembles the eS26:uS11 subcomplex into the pre-ribosome.
source: We show that the ATPase Fap7 promotes tertiary interactions between eS26 and uS11 and then concurrently assembles the eS26:uS11 subcomplex into the pre-ribosome.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence throughout the manuscript.

claim: Prefabrication of an r-protein subcomplex guarantees that stoichiometric levels of uS11 and eS26 are integrated into the 90S.
source: In this way, prefabrication of an r-protein subcomplex guarantees that stoichiometric levels of uS11 and eS26 are integrated into the 90S.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that Fap7 pre-organizes the uS11:eS26 complex before loading it onto the pre-ribosome.

claim: 40S pre-ribosomes assembled in Fap7- and Tsr2-depleted cells that lack both uS11 and eS26 efficiently escape nuclear proofreading and are transported to the cytoplasm.
source: 40S pre-ribosomes assembled in Fap7- and Tsr2-depleted cells that lack both uS11 and eS26 efficiently escape nuclear proofreading, and are transported to the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that Fap7-depletion does not impair pre-40S export (Figure 2C) and by previous studies on Tsr2-depletion.

claim: Incompletely assembled 40S subunits lacking uS11 and eS26 engage with mature 60S subunits to form 80S-like particles but fail to undergo final 20S pre-rRNA processing.
source: These incompletely assembled subunits engage with mature 60S subunits to form 80S-like particles, but fail to undergo final 20S pre-rRNA processing and accumulate in the cytoplasm (Schütz et al., 2014; Strunk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Proteomic analyses revealed an underrepresentation of eS26 and uS11 in 80S-like particles that accumulate upon Fap7-depletion.
source: Our findings are consistent with proteomic analyses that revealed an underrepresentation of eS26 and uS11 in these 80S-like particles that accumulate upon Fap7-depletion (Strunk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a previous study, supported by citation.

claim: The Fap7:uS11 complex with the assistance of RanGTP bypasses Tsr2-requirement in extracting eS26 from its importin in vitro.
source: The Fap7:uS11 complex with the assistance of RanGTP bypasses Tsr2-requirement in extracting eS26 from its importin in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: eS26 needs to be released from Tsr2 before engaging with the Fap7:uS11 complex.
source: eS26, when bound to Tsr2, was not recruited to the Fap7:uS11 complex, suggesting that eS26 needs to be released from Tsr2 before engaging with the Fap7:uS11 complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the Tsr2:eS26 complex does not interact with Fap7:uS11 (Figure 3A).

claim: Fap7 ATPase activity is not required to form a Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex.
source: While Fap7 ATPase activity is not required to form a Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex, ATP hydrolysis is critical to load uS11:eS26 onto H23 rRNA.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B demonstrating complex formation in the absence of ATP.

claim: ATP hydrolysis by Fap7 is critical to load uS11:eS26 onto H23 rRNA.
source: While Fap7 ATPase activity is not required to form a Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex, ATP hydrolysis is critical to load uS11:eS26 onto H23 rRNA.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 5B demonstrating that ATP is required for H23 rRNA recruitment.

claim: Fap7 scaffolds the uS11:eS26 complex formation and its ATPase activity regulates integration of this r-protein subcomplex into the 90S.
source: We therefore suggest that Fap7 scaffolds the uS11:eS26 complex formation and its ATPase activity regulates integration of this r-protein subcomplex into the 90S.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing Fap7-dependent complex formation and ATP-dependent loading onto rRNA.

claim: Fap7 loads the pre-formed uS11:eS26 complex during early nucleolar assembly of the 90S pre-ribosome.
source: Our data support a model in which Fap7 loads the pre-formed uS11:eS26 complex during early nucleolar assembly of the 90S pre-ribosome.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that uS11 and eS26 co-enrich with the 90S marker Noc4-TAP and that Fap7 is nuclear localized.

claim: The essential nature and enzymatic activity requirement for Fap7 function distinguishes it from dedicated chaperones such as Acl4.
source: The essential nature and enzymatic activity requirement for its function distinguishes Fap7 from another dedicated chaperones such as Acl4.
evidence: This is a comparison drawn between Fap7 and Acl4 based on their different mechanisms and requirements.

claim: The Acl4 chaperone system captures the r-protein uL4 in the cytoplasm for Kap104-mediated import.
source: The Acl4 chaperone system captures the r-protein uL4 in the cytoplasm for Kap104-mediated import. Subsequently, the interaction of the eukaryotic-specific uL4 extension with the pre-ribosomal surface is thought to trigger energy-independent disassembly of the Acl4:RpL4 complex and allow for incorporation of uL4 (Pillet et al., 2015; Stelter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Acl4 chaperone system, supported by citations.

claim: In wild-type cells, there are two pools of the Fap7:uS11 complex.
source: Based on the observation that co-overexpression of Fap7 and uS11 efficiently suppresses Tsr2-depletion phenotypes, we suggest that, in wild-type cells, there are two pools of the Fap7:uS11 complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that overexpression is required to compensate for Tsr2 loss, suggesting limiting amounts of free Fap7:uS11.

claim: The major pool of Fap7:uS11 complex performs the essential duty of organizing a Fap7:uS11:eS26 subcomplex and incorporating it into the 90S.
source: The major pool seems to perform the essential duty of organizing a Fap7:uS11:eS26 subcomplex and incorporating it into the 90S.
evidence: This is inferred from the essential nature of Fap7 and the observation that it is required for uS11 and eS26 incorporation into the 90S.

claim: Only a small pool of the Fap7:uS11 complex is available for its adjunct role in RanGTP-dependent unloading of eS26 directly from the importin.
source: Only a small pool of the Fap7:uS11 complex is available for its adjunct role in RanGTP-dependent unloading of eS26 directly from the importin and is therefore limiting in Tsr2-depleted cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that overexpression is required to compensate for Tsr2 loss.

claim: There are two mechanisms that operate to extract eS26 from the import machinery.
source: We propose two mechanisms that operate to extract eS26 from the import machinery.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on multiple lines of experimental evidence showing both Tsr2-dependent and Fap7:uS11-dependent pathways.

claim: The major RanGTP insensitive mechanism involves Tsr2 that extracts eS26 from the importin:eS26 complex and forms a stable Tsr2:eS26 complex.
source: The major RanGTP insensitive mechanism involves Tsr2 that extracts eS26 from the importin:eS26 complex, and forms a stable Tsr2:eS26 complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work and supported by the current findings.

claim: The alternative mechanism employs the preformed Fap7:uS11 complex for eS26 extraction from its importin.
source: The alternative mechanism employs the preformed Fap7:uS11 complex for eS26 extraction from its importin. In this case, the Fap7:uS11 interacts with eS26 when bound to its importin, and renders eS26 release RanGTP-sensitive.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assay data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Both mechanisms for eS26 extraction converge to form a Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex for incorporation into the 90S.
source: Importantly, both mechanisms converge to form a Fap7:uS11:eS26 complex for incorporation into the 90S.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that both pathways ultimately result in the same complex for ribosome assembly.

claim: Spatial clustering of ribosomal proteins through tertiary interactions is a striking structural feature of the eukaryotic ribosome.
source: Spatial clustering of ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) through tertiary interactions is a striking structural feature of the eukaryotic ribosome.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about eukaryotic ribosomes.

claim: Eukaryotic r-proteins cluster on the surface of the ribosome through a network of ~140 tertiary contacts.
source: A striking structural feature of eukaryotic r-proteins is that they cluster on the surface of the ribosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) through a network of ~140 tertiary contacts (Poirot and Timsit, 2016).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge, supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prefabricating r-protein subcomplexes through tertiary contacts prior to their assembly provides a mechanism to reduce the molecularity of the incorporation process.
source: Prefabricating r-protein subcomplexes through these tertiary contacts prior to their assembly provides one mechanism to reduce the molecularity of the incorporation process and ensure stoichiometric levels of r-proteins reach their rRNA binding sites.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the specific findings about Fap7-mediated prefabrication of the uS11:eS26 subcomplex.

claim: Fap7 may represent a family of factors that pre-organize native-like r-protein subcomplexes and minimize production errors during eukaryotic ribosome formation.
source: Thus, Fap7 may represent a family of factors that pre-organize native-like r-protein subcomplexes and minimize production errors during eukaryotic ribosome formation.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion extrapolating from the findings about Fap7 to suggest a broader principle in ribosome assembly.
